name: Yisroel Milstein
summary: Minnie’s paternal grandfather, married to Zisel. Documentary parentage for Chaya Dwora supplies matching Israel/Zissel names.

name: Zisel
summary: Minnie’s paternal grandmother. Minnie recalls her living with Israel Alter’s mother across the Bug. Maiden surname not established.

name: Leibish Milstein
summary: Father of Moshe, Nutke and Minnie; husband of Chaya Appelbaum. Minnie supplies his names and siblings.

name: Chaya Appelbaum
summary: Minnie’s mother and Moshe’s mother in the working tree; daughter of Zalman. Her parents and village require records.

name: Moshe Milstein
summary: Doba’s first husband; father of Arke, Riva, Ben and Philip. Went to South Africa before them, around 1929 in the tapes. The Morris certificate is a strong match, not a completed proof.
facts: The candidate death record estimates birth around 1893–1894 from age 41.
The original death date is 5 September; 6 September is registration, and the date in the memorial index.

name: Doba Lederer
aliases: Doba Milsztejn · Milstein · later Slot · Boba / Bobba
summary: Born in Opalin; travelled with three children in 1934. After Moshe’s death, relatives recall her work and determination to keep the family together. Later married Isaac Slot.
facts: Estate reference 2783/77; the full estate is outstanding.
Passport birth year 1895 differs from the age 38 in the 1934 manifest.

name: Aron Milstein
summary: The eldest child, explicitly named by Ben. Travelled ahead of Doba’s party. Family accounts describe long-term residential care; the institution and clinical history have not been established.
facts: The burial date is 20 February 1977, H 2215.
His death and Doba’s are twelve days apart, despite remembered intervals of ten or eleven.

name: Riva Gilinsky
summary: Doba and Moshe’s daughter; later wife of Max (Mackie) Gilinsky. The identification card records her birth and ship arrival. Masie is a family nickname confirmed by Mark.
facts: The 1934 manifest lists Rywka aged 14. The remembered age 16 on arrival conflicts with the card and manifest.
Ethan describes family hospitality, synagogue life and shared meals in Emmarentia.
Chevrah Kadisha register records death and burial on 1 June 2015; the 1938 marriage names Max Gilinsky.

name: Ben Milstein
summary: One of the three accompanying children. His interviews name the siblings and describe the journey, his father’s death, engineering work and life in Israel. Mark confirms Ben and his wife have died; dates remain unverified here.

name: Philip Milstein
summary: Youngest child on Doba’s passport and manifest. The group tapes preserve his childhood recollections, although a complete speaker map is not established. Mark confirms Philip and his wife have died.

name: Nutke Milstein
summary: Moshe’s brother, Minnie’s brother and Riva’s uncle. A portrait survives. No secure individual victim record or exact death place/date has been found.
facts: Do not assume his formal name was Natan merely because a search expands the nickname.
A separate maternal uncle Nutke Appelbaum appears in Minnie’s account.

name: Minnie Spitalnik
summary: Moshe’s younger sister, rather than Doba’s Lederer sister. Her recordings preserve much of the earlier family. A 1937 Mina Milstein–Elias Spitalnik marriage is a strong match.
facts: The gravestone gives Menucha daughter of Leib.
Arrival in 1936 is a recollection; a 1956 naturalisation/immigration index is not evidence of arrival that year.

name: George Spitalnik
aliases: George · candidate civil name Elias · filename label Eltzik
summary: Mark identifies Minnie’s husband as George and supplies their photograph together, confirming George as a family-used name. The strong 1937 marriage candidate calls the groom Elias Spitalnik, a Lithuania-born tailor. A further link is needed to establish whether George and Elias were names of the same man.

name: Max Gilinsky
summary: Riva’s husband, known as Mackie. Grew up in Upington after the family lived in Benoni. His 1938 marriage records him as a general dealer; Mark recalls his later Station Jewellers business in Mayfair. Read the Gilinsky branch.
facts: Exact birth date 1 October 1910 and Benoni birthplace remain family-tree claims; age 28 in the 1938 marriage supports the approximate year.
Burial register gives Hebrew name Mordecai son of Shlomo.

name: Aron Lederer
summary: Listed as Doba’s father in Ethan’s earlier Ancestry tree. No inspected parentage record confirms this.

name: Finkel
aliases: Full name and meaning of entry uncertain
summary: Shown beside Aron Lederer as Doba’s mother in the earlier tree. Do not assume Finkel is a verified maiden surname.

name: Binyomin Lederer
summary: Hela’s father is Binyomin in her burial patronymic. She says her father was Doba’s brother. Beniamin and Yosefa are named parents in the sister testimonies.

name: Yosefa Lederer
dates: Age 45 in testimony; no dated birth
summary: Strong candidate for Hela’s mother. Her original testimony lists three children, matching Hela’s household. Parents Eliezer and Chaya; sister Brakha Berland.
facts: Possible handwritten widow conflicts with the index’s married: reading provisional.
Do not turn age 45 into a birth year without a dated event.

name: Hela Lederer
summary: Doba’s niece and Riva’s cousin. Moved from Opalin to her uncle Mendel’s Warsaw household at twelve; later married Harry and joined him in southern Africa.

name: Harry Lederer
summary: Opalin-born builder in Hela’s account; left for South Africa in 1936 and moved to Bulawayo in 1937. Exact degree of any relationship to Hela before marriage is not established.

name: Frida / Freida Lederer
summary: Hela names a sister Frida. The Opalin testimony names parents Beniamin/Yosefa and husband Eliahu, with aunt Berka Berland as submitter. Strong candidate, not an explicit Hela sibling record.

name: Nechama? / Chuma?
summary: Hela’s other sister is transcribed Nechama. Chuma’s testimony has matching parents and place, husband Tzvi, married surname unknown. The two names have not been proved to identify one woman.

name: Mendel Lederer
dates: Born 1880 in one testimony; 1885 in another
summary: Hela’s uncle and a strong candidate for the Ogrodowa 24 baker. The two testimony records differ in birth year, occupation and death place and remain unmerged.

name: Pesl Sosne / Sosna
summary: Testimony: Opalin-born, husband Asher, daughter Ana Roiter. Minnie’s Sosna/Reuter recollections make this worth pursuing; the link to Doba is still unproved.

name: Emma Ray?
summary: Hela’s maternal aunt, not automatically a Lederer. Sent money and clothing after Hela’s father’s death. Her husband delivered coal.

name: Brakha Berland
summary: Submitter identified as Yosefa’s sister and the aunt of the women in the sister testimonies. A 29-result submitter-name search found no further explicit Hela or Doba link.

name: Chaya Dwora Alter
summary: Opalin-born, parents Israel and Zissel, husband Naftali. Strong converging case for Leibish’s sister and Israel Alter’s mother; the exact aunt-name on Minnie’s tape remains uncertain.

name: Naftali Alter
summary: Named as Chaya Dwora’s husband in her testimony. Same-name Dorohusk victim records have not been assigned to him.

name: Israel Alter
summary: Mark stayed with him in Tel Aviv in 1986. Strongly identified with the memoirist and filmmaker Naftali’s father. The memoir names his mother Chaya Dvora.

name: Pnina Alter
summary: Named as Naftali’s mother and Israel’s wife in the published interview; born Łódź in that account.

name: Naftali Alter
summary: Public professional identity confirmed by the Israel Film Archive; the interview names Israel and Pnina as parents. Proposed second cousin of Riva through the qualified older Milstein link.

name: Liba Malka
summary: Another daughter of Yisroel and Zisel in Minnie’s account. No secure married name or civil record yet.

name: Moshe Milstein, older generation
summary: Leibish’s brother, distinct from Doba’s husband Moshe.

name: David Milstein
summary: Leibish’s brother in Minnie’s account.

name: Zalman Appelbaum
summary: Chaya Appelbaum’s father. Minnie names his parents approximately Leibu and Rochel; she tentatively gives his wife’s name as Rochel too.

name: Isaac Slot
aliases: Isaac G. Slot in earlier tree
summary: Doba’s second husband and stepfather of the Milstein children. A candidate earlier household names wife Annie and three children. The later marriage record and full estate are outstanding.

name: Annie Slot
summary: Edinburgh-born, father Gerson Camberg, married to an Isaac Slot described as estate agent. Candidate earlier household of Doba’s later husband.

name: Paul Slot
summary: Remembered Slot stepfamily member; Paul appears in the Annie notice. The identification is plausible but not yet fully joined across records.

name: Nick Slot
summary: Ben remembers an unmarried son Nick. Ethan’s tree calls Leslie Nick; Annie’s notice names Leslie, born 16 May 1923. This is a useful fit, not yet a proved alias.

name: Hayme / Hymie Slot?
aliases: Helman C. may be a duplicate in the old tree
summary: The original notice’s Hayme reading is provisional. Ethan’s tree shows both Helman C. and Hymie with identical 1917–1981 dates; do not count them as two confirmed children or identify a sister from these entries.

name: Phyllis
summary: Hela supplies her daughter’s birth date and describes their June 1938 voyage to join Harry. A manifest and civil birth record remain to be checked.

name: Shlomo Gilinsky
summary: Max’s father, identified by Mark in photographs. His Upington store sign names S. Gilinsky, General Dealer. Matching civil death and burial records give ages 80 and 79; the tree’s 1885 birth conflicts.

name: Leah Gilinsky
summary: Mother in the family tree. Leah Dinah Gilinsky, born Nasatir, appears in the 1918 court catalogue and a 1920 remarriage; the direct link to Max is still unconfirmed. Anne Spiro’s estate index names mother Lea.

name: Solly Gilinsky
summary: Max’s brother, identified by Mark. Gravestone names father Shlomo and wife Sarah; a marriage index names Sarah Gayer.

name: Sarah Gilinsky
summary: Solly’s wife; stone names father Eliyahu. Gayer appears in marriage index and Geyer in Gidon Katz’s recollection, which connects her to the Ochberg group.

name: Milly Gilinsky Katz
summary: Gidon Katz identifies Milly as his mother, Benoni-born and raised in Upington, one of six Gilinsky siblings. Her husband Max Katz is a different person from Max Gilinsky.

name: Annie Gilinsky Spiro
summary: 1929 Upington marriage names Jack Spiro. A candidate estate index names parents Solomon and Lea Gilinsky, birth in Benoni (indexed Bononi), and husband Jacob Spiro.

name: Edith Gilinsky Lang
summary: Gazette establishes maiden surname Gilinsky and Rand Leases, Florida residence. Stone names father Shlomo. Strong candidate for Max’s sister; marriage to Morris remains unlocated.

name: Fanny Gilinsky Lang
summary: Married Bennie Lang in Johannesburg in 1937; stone names father Shlomo. Strong candidate for Max’s sister.

name: Bennie Lang
summary: Married Fanny Gilinsky in 1937; gravestone explicitly names wife Fanny. The brother mentioned on his stone is unnamed.
